"Triple Red 7s Multiplier" has had no $77,777 top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

If you play "Triple Red 7s Multiplier" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
802.headline: Top prizes are still left

803.body:
"Triple Red 777s" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of its unclaimed prize money, about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

If "Triple Red 777s" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.

804.headline: Good news: no big claims

805.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Multiply Your Money", about half are still unsold. The game is about halfway through its run, with four of seven top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Every line of Multiply Your Money's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.

807.headline: No new top prize claims

808.body:
"Ravens X10" has three of four top prizes left and is near the midpoint of its run. About a third of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Everything above about "Ravens X10" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.

810.headline: The prize table, line by line

811.body:
The key fact about "Extreme Green" is how its eleven prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward the smaller prizes. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

Today's free summary of "Extreme Green" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.

817.headline: Early stage or late

818.body:
"10X Cash" is near the start of its run, with most of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The numbers for "10X Cash" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
